issues.description: Template code does not compile due to inconsistent ArrayHelpers method naming: template ArrayHelpers defines appendElement(T[], T) but template Stock.addToStockIngredients(...) calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...), which does not exist in the template. The solution uses addElementToArray(...), so students starting from the template will get a compilation error in Stock.java.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the helper method name consistent across template and solution. E.g., rename template ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...), or change template Stock.addToStockIngredients(...) to call appendElement(...). Ensure all call sites use the same name.

issues.description: Contradictory specification for SealSaloon.stock: the problem statement says SealSaloon has a "final Stock stock" initialized in the constructor (instance field), but also explicitly requires the stock attribute (and acceptSupplyDelivery/calculateTotalPrice) to be static (shared across all instances). This inconsistency makes it unclear whether stock should be per-instance final or class-level static final.
issues.suggestedFix: Decide on one design and make all artifacts match. If stock is shared, specify and show "private static final Stock stock" and keep acceptSupplyDelivery/calculateTotalPrice static. If stock is per saloon, remove the static requirements and keep "private final Stock stock" initialized in the constructor; update UML/text accordingly.

issues.description: Solution output for calculateRemainingOrderNumber() is off by one compared to the problem statement: the statement defines n as the remaining order number (i.e., remaining orders) and expects printing "Order number: 0" up to "Order number: n". In the solution, remainingOrders is set to this.orders.length + 1 and the loop prints 0..orders.length+1, producing one extra line beyond the remaining order count.
issues.suggestedFix: Align loop bounds with the intended meaning of "remaining order number". For example: set int remainingOrders = this.orders.length; then use a do-while to print 0..remainingOrders inclusive (or adjust condition) without adding an extra +1.
